speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old woman. The patient noticed a mass in her left breast 4 weeks ago, which has rapidly increased in size. She denies any recent trauma or infections. No history of similar complaints in the past.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has this mass been associated with any skin changes like dimpling, redness, or nipple retraction on the left side? Also, do you notice any clear or bloody discharge from the nipple?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Presence of a left breast mass. I also have Rapid increase in size of the mass, No skin or nipple changes, No pain associated with the mass.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for those details. Given the rapid growth of the mass without pain or skin changes, is there any history of hormonal issues or recent pregnancy? Also, have you noticed any lumps in your armpit area?

REQUEST TEST: Ultrasound of the left breast and axilla.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ultrasound: A 6-cm, nontender, multinodular mass with rapid growth in the left breast. No palpable axillary lymphadenopathy. Internal echoes suggest a complex cystic component with possible septations.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound shows a complex, rapidly enlarging mass; have you noticed any recent weight changes, night sweats, or bone pain? Also, does the mass feel distinct from the surrounding breast tissue or does it seem fixed? REQUEST TEST: Serum Tumor Markers (CA 15-3, CA 125).

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Phyllodes Tumor (likely benign or borderline given normal tumor markers and lack of skin fixation, though rapid growth and large size warrant excision).
